author: LuciferYang
body:
`commit_compaction` cleans up the data files a failed commit left behind (#6320) but not the `_indices/{uuid}/` directories written before that commit, by `remap_indices` and by the fragment-reuse index build. Those directories belong to no version, so a conservative `cleanup_old_versions` leaves them for `UNVERIFIED_THRESHOLD_DAYS`, and a workload that keeps losing the commit race accumulates them. That is the half of #7207 still open: the reporter saw a compaction lose to a concurrent delete, strand ~3.5G of data and ~3.1G of indices, and a table directory grow from 26G to 71G in a day.

This collects the index ids the transaction minted, before they move into the transaction, and removes their directories on the failure path.

Only ids that differ from the index they replace are eligible. `remap_indices` reports an index it chose not to rewrite as `RemapResult::Keep` with `new_id == old_id`, which points at the directory the committed manifest still uses; deleting that would break every query that scans the index. Cleanup is best-effort: a fragment-reuse index that inlines its details writes no directory, so a missing one is expected, and any other error is logged rather than masking the commit error the caller needs.

## Tests

Three cases, each verified to fail without the corresponding line of the fix:

- `test_commit_compaction_cleans_up_indices_on_commit_failure` — the remap directory is reclaimed. Without the cleanup call, `_indices/` keeps two directories instead of one.
- `test_commit_compaction_keeps_index_dirs_it_did_not_write` — an id reported as kept survives. Without the `new_id != old_id` filter, the live directory is deleted.
- `test_commit_compaction_cleans_up_frag_reuse_index_on_commit_failure` — the fragment-reuse directory is reclaimed under `defer_index_remap` with details past the inline threshold. Without the `frag_reuse_index` term, that directory leaks.

Directories are compared as a set of names rather than a count, so deleting the wrong one cannot pass. Each case pins the failure to the injected commit error, so a change that fails compaction earlier cannot leave the test vacuously green.

`cargo test -p lance --lib dataset::optimize` (115 passed), `cargo clippy -p lance --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc -p lance --no-deps`, and `cargo fmt --all --check` all pass.

## Out of scope

- `remap_indices` failing part-way returns before this block, so directories an earlier index in that loop already wrote still leak. Same orphan class, different failure site.
- A rebase inside `apply_commit` can mint a new fragment-reuse uuid after this snapshot is taken; that directory is not covered. Fixing it needs `apply_commit` to report the uuids it wrote.
- A commit handler that fails after the manifest reached its final path — a `CommitLock` whose release errors, for instance — breaks the assumption that `Err` means "not committed". The existing data-file cleanup makes the same assumption, and the doc comment on `cleanup_index_dirs` states it as a precondition rather than a guarantee.
